Title: Forced re-authentication on first post-migration login (server-side Redis session destruction)

Record only observable effects (Redis session destruction is a server mechanism, not directly visible).
Actual UI Observation (Verbatim): The app authenticates via Google SSO (OIDC to accounts.google.com / auth.staging.shopview.com) backed by server-side session cookies (PHPSESSID + sv_sso_session). Two directly-observable effects were recorded: (1) SESSION INVALIDATION ON IDENTITY SWITCH — performing the DEV MODE 'Tech' quick-login on a context that shared the same PHPSESSID as the active admin session rebound/destroyed the prior admin session server-side: immediately afterward, admin API calls (GET /api/roles, GET /api/roles/{id}) began returning HTTP 403 and the admin roles-permissions page failed to load, requiring re-authentication (re-clicking the 'Admin' quick-login restored access). (2) NO ISOLATED SECOND SESSION WITHOUT SSO — attempting to establish an independent Tech session in a separate cookie jar (cf_clearance only, no shared sv_sso_session) caused the 'Tech' quick-login to redirect to the real Google sign-in page (accounts.google.com), which is out of scope (no Google SSO automation). Consequently a clean concurrent two-session test (a live independent Tech session + a separate admin role change) could NOT be completed in-browser. The server-side Redis session destruction itself is not visible in the UI; only the above HTTP-403 invalidation and the SSO redirect were observable.
If No/Partial — What the UI Says Instead: Observable server-side session invalidation exists (prior session -> HTTP 403 after an identity switch, forcing re-auth), consistent with the described mechanism, but the specific 'admin changes Tech's role -> Tech's live session forced to re-auth' scenario could not be isolated in-browser because a second independent login requires Google SSO (out of scope). No toast is involved (as the case notes).

Actual UI Observation (Verbatim): ROLE EDITOR (verbatim): toggle label = 'View and Manage AP/AR Data'; subtitle = 'Controls visibility of unpaid invoices, payments and credits tabs on customer and vendor pages. Without this setting the following fields are hidden on the Edit Customer modal: Credit terms, Credit limit, Default Labor rate, Default Shop Supplies, Min and Max, Taxes, PO is required.' Named sensitive fields (7): Credit terms, Credit limit, Default Labor rate, Default Shop Supplies, Min and Max, Taxes, PO is required. TECH BEHAVIOR (logged in as Tech ShopView with AP/AR toggle OFF, role granted Customers View+Create&Edit only): (a) EDIT CUSTOMER MODAL — opening customer 'A 2 Company' > 'edit_note' opens the 'Edit Customer' modal which shows ONLY: Name*, Phone, Address 1, Address 2, City, ZIP/Postal Code, State/Province, Country, Sales Representative, Notes, Website, IBS, 'Pin notes?', Save. ALL 7 named AP/AR fields are ABSENT (hidden) from the Edit Customer modal — consistent with the subtitle claim. (b) CUSTOMER DETAIL PAGE — however, the customer detail left-info panel STILL shows two of the named fields to Tech with AP/AR OFF: 'Credit term: DOR' and 'Credit limit: $NaN'. So the AP/AR gate hides the 7 fields on the Edit Customer modal (as claimed) but does NOT hide Credit term/Credit limit on the customer detail page — the gate is not comprehensive across all customer surfaces (front-end gating limited to the Edit modal).
If No/Partial — What the UI Says Instead: On the Edit Customer modal all 7 named fields ARE hidden (subtitle accurate). BUT the AP/AR toggle's claim is scoped only to the Edit Customer modal: the customer DETAIL page left panel still exposes 'Credit term' (DOR) and 'Credit limit' ($NaN) to a user with AP/AR OFF — i.e. the gate does not hide those fields everywhere.
